Really cool game. Follows the real rules of Yu-Gi-Oh. Brings out nostalgia and is genuinely fun to play. Collect cards, build a deck using one of the many archetypes like red-eyes black dragon, dark magician, etc, etc. I also feel like it's very free-to-play friendly, and you can easily build your first favourite deck. You can craft cards, open packs, play solo mode and multiplayer duels. Would highly recommend. The playstyles are diverse and unlike Hearthstone, cards never become obsolete in ranked 1v1. You can play the newest cards and oldest cards.

Give it a try!

This is Yu-Gi-Oh, a very honest recreation of what the modern game is like and all that entails. Suped up with great animations and a very impressively generous headstart system, this is the best way to play the game online and has made me fall back in love with it.

with the starting currency you can make a full competitive deck and still have enough leftover to plan your next.

Terrible tutorials. I've never seen a game spend so much time hand holding you on how to actually do an action, and then completely ignore the why. It's akin to learning to bake via only pre-made recipe cards, then throwing you into a cooking competition. I believe it's to farm new players for their playerbase. Who cares that I give up on the game after x number of games, as long as the players who pay got to win x number of times.

I like the game play, just needs better process for new players to get started

If you think you are gonna download this game to have a fun time dueling let me tell you now you aren't. Unless you are ready to go full sweat lord to win entire duels in 1 to 2 turns then stay away. Played 4 matches had a total of 8 turns between all 4 matches was about 3 hours irl watched 4 different people make about 30-40's actions in one turn. I literally started surrendering matches because some players single turns would last 45 mins to and hour before you ever even got the chance to start playing yourself. FUCK THIS GAME NEW YUGIOH IS ASS!!!!!!!!!

Yugioh is fundamentally a flawed game. Biggest problem is that its semi-solved from turn one. This means that if you could look in your opponents hand, you could say who wins that match. This shows games lack of interaction and player choice-most matches finish by turn one simply by one player going comboing with all his cards in hand utilising most of his deck and then negating everything other player does. People mistake this for some complex high iq game but reality is that this is just a game for people who memorise 2-3 slightly different patterns of card effects which lead to more or less same result-other player losing the game at spot. Stay away.

Much better than the other yu-gi-oh games i have played so far. My only problem is playing "ranked" games where supposedly you fight against people the "same" rank as you, only to fight some japanese or chinese player spend eternity in one turn to summon everything in their deck and counter all counters you set up which turns you into a spectator and then just destroy you...... they should fix the ranked game system. Still, good game.

I really thought people were exaggerating about this being a waiting simulator, a spectator game, just watching your opponent playing but man. Just spent the last 30 min on the second turn of my opponent just playing card after card after card but waiting a few min between each and I just gave up trying to play this game. I remember Yugioh being actually fun back in the day and pretty simple to play. Now you need a freaking PhD it seems to play it.

The game itself looks great tho, the animations and all looks good. But I would've preferred to have a chance to play the game against AI opponents for a bit to get a hang of the game and also have a chance to get gems to then play against real players but this game seems to be if you aren't willing to open up your wallet at the very start and most likely spend a few hundreds, if not thousands of dollars to make a deck that works right from the start, this game isn't for you. If you are using a pre built deck, all you'll get is loss after loss.

This is probably the most non-predatory F2P game I've tried and it's from fucking Konami. You can trade in cards you don't want to buy a specific one of the same rarity you want at a 3:1 rate, buying an Ultra Rare will get you a free roll on its pack so you can roll for the rest of the archetype, and if your tenroll doesn't drop a UR you'll be guaranteed one on your next one. The tutorial's skippable for fast rerolls, there's no dailies besides starting up the game, no paywall, and the game just vomits gems at you. The most offensive thing I've seen is that archetype packs only unlock for 24 hours after getting an SR or UR from them, but that gets refreshed whenever you get a card from them.

Secrets of Eternity was released in January 2015. This set introduced the Infernoids, a series of monsters that can Special Summon themselves to the field by banishing other Infernoids from either the hand or graveyard. Notable cards in set include Farfa, Malebranche of the Burning Abyss, Qliphort Monolith, Uni-Zombie, Nephe Shaddoll Fusion, and a card that would bolster Satellarknight to combat the Burning Abyss Shaddoll meta, Stellarknight Constellar Diamond. In this series, both Nyhmnim and myself will be opening 24 booster packs or 1 box of a core Yu-Gi-Oh! booster set. We will build a deck and play a best 2 out of 3, and the winner will receive a small prize to upgrade their deck. H O W E V E R each episode, we will open another box of the next set that was released moving in chronological order, constantly upgrading our decks before dueling each other at the end of each episode. This is the Yu-Gi-Oh! Progression Series.

It's stupid that there are cards now that straight up can't be destroyed via magic or trap cards but can be summoned turn 1 and start with 3000 atk even toon terror which negates and destroys a card cannot destroy the card but will still negate the effect then on top of that the card can destroy any of your cards once per turn and gets +1000 atk from it. wtf is yugioh doing?

Only driving factor for me to keep playing was that I was a fan of the anime. As far as card games go, this is the one game where you will have to wait for your opponent to play for the longest. It gets very tedious to watch people do "link summons", and play 15-20 cards each turn, especially at the start of the Duel. There have been Duels where I had to wait for 4 minutes before I can play any cards. Every new card has obnoxious effects like "destroy one monster that your opponent controls each round, or you can negate an effect each round." Sorry, I fail to see the fun in this. I really prefer the old gameboy advance games over this one purely because I didn't have to wait for minutes every round, and the cards I played matter because every deck was not full of silly effects that erased all of my board just because the opponent was able to "link summon" a card at the end of 4 minutes of continuous summoning from their extra deck. If you find chess boring, you would miss chess after playing this game for few hours.

I don't ever play games like this. However, a friend of mine convinced me to download it and learn how to play. I have now played it for nearly 12 hours! It's really fun and teaches you how to play very well and detailed. 10/10 recommend it!

Too much to learn get into. It kind of reminds me of fighting games. Or any competitive game in general.

I think the game is pretty balanced, there isn't anything that seemed unfair to me. The art is pretty cool so I think if you have time you can pick a theme you like and go with a viable deck for it. My only problem is not with the game really, it's rather with me; I have more and more work on my lap and less and less time to play, so when I play I want to have some quick fun. I have already learned what the game ask me to do, I just know that I will have to practice for quite a while before getting somewhere where I would like to be, and nowadays the idea of doing that doesn't appeal to me anymore.

Still, if you have some times on your hands, don't give up at the first hurdle. The basics are not chess-level for sure, but the depth isn't chess-level either; you will manage with practice in much less time than you think I am sure.

I stopped playing YGO when XYZs came out. I started to see how exagerated and unbalanced the game started to be (yeah, even more than before). Too expensive, too. I still knew what was going on through friends: Pendulum, in my opinion, killed the game.

Got Duel Links a time ago, it was fun, it was kind-of balanced. I got bored with the time passing.

Got this to see how is it going, because I still have that "inner flame", you know... Well, I'm in ROOKIE level and got wrecked by a dude who summoned like 9 monsters in one turn, 7 with more text than my most boring history book on high school.

I remembered why I quitted YGO and uninstalled.

This game is for competitive players mostly, I wouldn't mind the grinding necessary for making a deck if I didnt have to worry about running into Eld or Swordsoul every 3 duels. And this is why not having a casual ladder (or a casual matching system) is such a big deal to me.

Also the free to play aspect of this game IS an improvement over usual systems (and kudos to Konami for that, I wholeheartedly wish to see more games with this type of crafting mechanic in play in the future), but the fact that you can't buy crafting points directly and instead have to rely on the pack opening lottery to get them is such a low blow.

Oh yeah also, this game is fucking dogshit at explaining YGO with it's solo modes, shit would've worked so great if they had them be worked in a way where you showcased mechanics instead of random ass archetypes that haven't been relevant in forever. Teach people to link and xyz, not how fucking Elementsabers and bloody Karakuris work. This is a very complex and convoluted game, if you don't teach newcomers how to play you won't be getting newcomers at all, and the game will keep it's bad rep.

I love Yu-Gi-Oh!, I love modern Yu-Gi-Oh!, I'm a casual player, and this just isn't the YGO experience I'm looking for. I'm sticking to the older sims and physical play.

Overall I love the game, however, I would love them to make an option where when you are looking for opponents, it can be customized. For example, I played the old-fashioned Yugioh where the furthest I go is 2nd gen. If they make something like that would be great. Cause the new Yugioh nowdays, 1 move takes 5-10 min long. That's why I stop playing after almost 20 hours cause I realize I can't do it no more.

This game got the true essence of Yu-Gi-Oh TCG, the pay-to-win factor, that is. They even got Rare Holo cards in here, also with abysmally low rates in the booster packs.

Cards are ranked with rarity; the more "meta" the card is, the higher the rarity, and the more you have to spend/dismantle to get a decent deck in order to win a match.

Booster packs for specific cards can only be made available and bought if you unlock the secret pack, which requires you to either: buy a pack and get a card from the secret pack, or craft an SR from an archetype, both of which is not sustainable unless you follow very strict guides.

OCG ruling for ranked matches, can't even use/craft banned cards to use against friends on a special rules match.

Stagnating meta and desperate players wanting to win a game using expensive cheese decks makes this TCG simulator not fun for beginners and F2P alike. Can't even re-roll your first 10.000 gems if you're playing from Steam.

(Big rewards for new players) So if you can live with no chance against almost anyone, go 4 it- You will be frustrated. New players- RUN!!!!

It's so simple even a third-rate duelist could figure it out.

Yugioh is fun, this is not fun. This is only fun if you only and exclusively play with your friends, or "fun" if you pay to win. By "fun" I mean spending 30 minutes setting up a board so you opponent doesn't and can't do anything. So it just ends with a surrender

Only bother with this game if you plan to play with friends.

Ranked play is less fun that eating sand and packs are expensive, and there's no quickplay casual mode. Just ranked.

An absolute blast to play, for those who are unsure about a deck to play check out master duel meta. My only issues with the game are that the solo mode rewards are a bit too small outside of the tutorial and first practice and to do well online you basically have to use the meta or the anti-meta decks. Apart from that great game

Yugioh seems fun enough with very simple cards but you don’t often get that experience because the singleplayer is pretty much all tutorial (and it’s VERY scripted) and the multiplayer leads to incredibly imbalanced games where you get assblasted by a dragonmaid deck after waiting 20 minutes for the other player’s first turn to end only to be greeted by a card only topped by the highest combo manageable in the starter deck (which RNG isn’t going to let you have).

If every card ability descriptions exceeds 3 paragraphs then every turn takes an hour to comprehend. And if I see an opponent with zero cards in hand and zero monsters or traps on the field I better be able to attack directly without a 20 minute intermission as my opponent pulls out a dark magicians combo out of their ass/graveyard/hole of banishment

Absolutely Love this game truly one of the best adaptations of Yugioh ever made. Theirs So much Deck variety being able to play with friends in lobby and team duels and the events are a great way to learn about new arch types. I 100% recommend this game to anyone who is a fan of Yugioh or just looking for a good strategy or card game but can't afford it in real life.
